thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT • Dedicated pool 'eu-dedicated-1' ingress surge detected, autoscaler falling behind, queue depth > 1200, p95 latency 1.2s, errors spiking (~4%). Trigger: capacity-critical.

maria (oncall): seeing it too. Large spike starting ~2795006500. Most requests are chat/generation. Dedicated pool cpu/gpu utilization at ~98%.

sam (eng-runtime): confirming autoscaler logs show PendingPods backlog, scaling attempts queued but kube can't attach new GPUs fast enough. Querying cloud quota now.

maria (oncall): customer-facing impact: multiple mid-market customers reporting timeouts; support case IDs: CS-6721, CS-6723. @anya, can you triage which customers have SLAs?

anya (support): on it. CS-6721 is enterprise (SLA), CS-6723 is dev-tier. Filing incident tags. I'll DM account owners.

sam (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations we can do now (fast):
- toggle burst capacity override for eu-dedicated-1 (temp)
- apply short-term rate limiting policy to new sessions (20% shed)
- disable streaming (reduce token churn) for non-SLA customers
- raise per-customer concurrent quota for SLA customers only

sam (eng-runtime): command to enable burst override (internal):
```bash
redwoodctl dedicated set-burst --pool eu-dedicated-1 --override on --duration 30m
```
(also requires auth: --auth-token from vault)

maria (oncall): I'd say enable burst override + gateway rate limit. Burst override should give ~2x immediate headroom but is finite. Liam, can you flip the gateway rules?

liam (sre): I can push a temporary route filter now. Plan:
1) Add gateway rule to reduce new session acceptance for non-enterprise: weight 0.8 (20% shed)
2) Patch quota service to keep enterprise customers above baseline
3) Enable burst override as Sam described

liam (sre): running gateway change:
```json
{
  "action":"modify_route",
  "route":"/v1/generate",
  "conditions": {"customer_tier":"non-enterprise"},
  "weight": 0.8
}
```
(Pushing now)

ops-bot: deploy-bot started: gateway-rule/2795006789 applied by liam. CI check OK.

maria (oncall): Sam, please enable burst. I'll open a temporary incident channel for postmortem notes.

sam (eng-runtime): running redwoodctl now (sudo):
```bash
# enabling 30m override
redwoodctl dedicated set-burst --pool eu-dedicated-1 --override on --duration 30m --reason "ingress surge - emergency"
```

ops-bot: command accepted. Burst override enabled on eu-dedicated-1 by sam. Expected headroom: +1.8x for 30m.

maria (oncall): metrics: queue depth dropping from 1200 -> 400 in last 2m. p95 latency down to 480ms. Errors down to 1.6%. Good signal.

anya (support): letting customers know: CS-6721 owner updated, we applied prioritized capacity; they see degraded but recovering. CS-6723 advised to retry.

liam (sre): additional step: I'm patching throttles at api-gateway for heavy token-consuming routes. This will reduce token generation concurrency.

sam (eng-runtime): note: autoscaler still healthy-ish but slow; need medium-term: scale up pool template (add nodes), but that's slower (10-20m). For now burst + rate-limits bought time.

maria (oncall): assignment: sam -> incident owner for debugging autoscaler lag. liam -> mitigation owner (gateway + quotas). anya -> customer comms. I'll tag postmortem owner after stabilization.

sam (eng-runtime): initial hypothesis: kube attach latency + cloud GPU allocation throttling; also saw repeated attach failures ~2795006600-2795006800. I'll collect kube logs and cloud API traces.

liam (sre): FYI, I patched the 'dedicated-burst-fallback' flag to allow LIFO draining (reduces cold-start overhead). Will monitor for side effects.

maria (oncall): next oncall handoff at 20:00 UTC. If storm persists, we'll keep it as critical.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE • 15m since trigger. Current status: mitigated (partial). Active mitigations: burst-override (eu-dedicated-1), gateway-rate-limit (non-enterprise 20%), quota-prioritization (enterprise).

anya (support): customers updated: CS-6721 marked "priority mitigated". No immediate escalations.

maria (oncall): preparing summary for ops postmortem: short bullets of timeline, mitigations, customer impact, commands run, owners. Sam - please paste autoscaler logs to this thread when ready.

sam (eng-runtime): will do. attaching key snippets:
```
[2795006702] autoscaler: scale attempt 3 -> reason: pendingPods backlog
[2795006710] cloud: attachGpu timeout 120s -> retrying
[2795006758] autoscaler: failed attach count=4, backing off 30s
```

liam (sre): spike seems to originate from a partner integration hitting retries; opened ticket with partner. Throttle applied to partner's API key as well.

maria (oncall): excellent. I'm going to hand off to @liam for the next 40m. Keep thread updated. If anything regresses, escalate to eng-plat.

liam (sre): ack. Taking over. Leaving note: verify burst metrics and make sure we don't oversubscribe.

maria (oncall): handing off (oncall -> liam) 19:42 UTC.

liam (sre): final note: we should add a runbook step to prefer burst override + gateway-shed for similar ingress spikes. Filing runbook PR: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-traffic-mitigation (will link in postmortem).

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVE PROVISIONAL • Monitoring for 30m. If stable, will move to resolved and create postmortem ticket.
